text.title: Internal Link Audit Failure Modes
text.summary: Six antipatterns observed when running internal-link audits. Each pairs symptom + root-cause + concrete fix and maps to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: The audit lists an entire section (all /guides/ pages, every paginated archive) as orphans; the pages are clearly linked from a JavaScript-rendered menu or sit behind a robots.txt disallow.

root-cause.source: Screaming Frog SEO Spider documentation; Google Search Central, JavaScript SEO

antipattern.root-cause: The crawl was run without JavaScript rendering, or with a scope narrower than the sitemap, and the page count was never reconciled.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-crawl-scope-reconciled: rerun with rendering enabled and the full host in scope, compare crawled indexable count to sitemap and CMS counts, explain every gap larger than 5 percent before computing any orphan or hub.

antipattern.symptom: Every page shows 300 or more incoming links; the "least linked" page has 280; the audit finds zero orphans and no rewire plan on a site where most articles are reachable only from the footer.
antipattern.root-cause: Incoming counts were taken from the raw inlinks total, which is dominated by sitewide navigation and footer links present on every page.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-incoming-count-excludes-boilerplate: split counts by link position, compute orphans and hubs on the contextual column only, and report the navigation column separately.

antipattern.symptom: The report contains a table of 40 orphan URLs and the finding "orphans should be linked"; the next quarterly audit lists the same 40 URLs.

root-cause.source: Widely established practice in technical SEO audit delivery

antipattern.root-cause: The audit stopped at detection; no page was assigned a rewire, redirect or deindex decision with a source page and anchor.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-orphan-gets-a-decision and r-rewire-item-fully-specified: one decision per orphan, and for every rewire decision a pasteable item with source URL, anchor text, placement and a named person.

antipattern.symptom: The content calendar declares a pillar with 12 cluster pages; the link matrix shows 3 cluster pages linking to the pillar and the pillar linking to none of them; the pillar ranks below its own cluster pages for the head term.
antipattern.root-cause: Cluster membership was tracked in a spreadsheet, not in the link graph; nobody checked reciprocity after publishing.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-pillar-cluster-reciprocity: build the pillar-to-cluster and cluster-to-pillar matrix per cluster, turn every missing edge into a rewire item, and flag pillars with fewer than 5 contextual cluster links as structurally incomplete.

antipattern.symptom: The anchor-text table for the top target page reads: "read more" 84, "click here" 31, "https://..." 12; or the rewire plan adds 40 links to one page all with the identical exact-match phrase.

root-cause.source: Google Search Central, link best practices

antipattern.root-cause: Links were generated by a template component or by a keyword brief rather than written into the sentence that references the target.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-anchor-text-descriptive: replace generic anchors with descriptive ones drawn from the target page's topic, vary wording across new links, and re-report the distribution after the rewire.

antipattern.symptom: Thousands of internal links point at pre-migration URLs that 301 to the current ones; some templates add rel="nofollow" to internal links; the rewire plan itself uses redirecting URLs as targets.

root-cause.source: Screaming Frog response codes report; Google Search Central, Evolving nofollow (2019)

antipattern.root-cause: The link inventory was never checked for final resolution, and a legacy template setting was applied sitewide without review.
antipattern.fix: Apply r-link-targets-final-url: list every link into 3xx, 4xx, 5xx, noindex, non-self-canonical or nofollow as a hygiene finding, and point every rewire item at the final indexable URL.

section.title: Human checkpoint
section.p: Before any binding action driven by an Internal Link Audit output (publish, send, rollout, commit), a named human reviewer must sign off. The agent surfaces a `ready_for_review=true` flag and does NOT auto-commit decisions, copy, configs, or rollouts.
